messages.subject: bym2  inla.posterior.sample  control quantization?
parts:
Hello INLA gurus. 

I am working on a bym2 model. I am trying to create bivariate plots of the joint posterior of some hyperparameters (phi vs sigma in the example below) via inla.posterior.sample.  The marginals look good. However, the posterior simulations seem to be quantized/discretized. Instead, I am hoping to get a more even distribution (nondiscretized version) as one might obtain from MCMC. How might I be able to obtain a more even sample distribution? Thanks!

The example below is taken directly from the "Germany example" using bym2 obtained from (http://www.r-inla.org/examples/case-studies), more specifically:



#####################################################################
## the Germany example  http://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/case-studies/pc-prior/bym/runme.R


data(Germany)
g = "germany.graph"
n = dim(Germany)[1]
Q = INLA:::inla.pc.bym.Q(g)
Q = INLA:::inla.scale.model(Q, constr=list(A=matrix(1, 1, n), e=0))

u = 0.2/0.31
alpha = 0.01
phi.u = 0.5
phi.alpha = 2/3 ## prob(phi < phi.u) = phi.alpha

phi.prior = INLA:::inla.pc.bym.phi(Q=Q, u= phi.u, alpha = phi.alpha)
values = (-9):110
values = 1:100
bym_hyper = list(
  phi = list( prior="pc", param=c(phi.u, phi.alpha), initial = -3), 
  prec = list( prior="pc.prec", param = c(u, alpha), initial = 5)
)
rw2_hyper = list(prec=list( prior="pc.prec", param=c(u, alpha)))
                
formula = Y ~ 1 
  + f(region, model="bym2", graph=g, scale.model=TRUE, constr=TRUE, hyper=bym_hyper) 
  + f(x, model="rw2", values=values, scale.model=TRUE, hyper=rw2_hyper)

r = inla(formula, data=Germany, family="poisson", E=E,
  control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),
  control.compute=list(config = TRUE)
)

r = r.germany = inla.hyperpar(r, dz = .5, diff.logdens=15)


## --------
## to this point, the code is identical to the tutorial/example


## simulation of joint posterior:
ps = inla.posterior.sample(n=1000, r)

hyper_names  = names(ps[[1]]$hyperpar )

i_phi = grep("Phi for region", hyper_names, fixed=TRUE )
i_sigma = grep("Precision for region", hyper_names, fixed=TRUE )

phi = sapply( ps, function(o) {o$hyperpar[[i_phi]] } )
sigma = sapply( ps, function(o) {1/sqrt(o$hyperpar[[i_sigma]])} )

# histograms are not smooth distributions
hist(phi, breaks=100 )  
hist(sigma, breaks=100 )

# scatterplot I am trying to obtain .. looks to be discretized .. how to make more even  
plot( phi ~ sigma )

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] bym2 inla.posterior.sample control quantization?
parts:
Hi,

with inla.posterior.sample(), only the integration points for the
hyperparameters in the INLA approximation
are used as sample candidates. If you need more complete samples for
the hyperparameters (but not simultaneously the latent variables), you
can use inla.hyperpar.sample() instead.

Finn
